subject: NovaAI dedicated sizing — balance memory-bound batch with L4 low-latency fallbacks
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir@novaai.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated sizing request + forecast attached

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for taking this. Attaching our Q3 demand forecast (CSV) and the SLA pdf. High level: we expect two major workload patterns —

1) Heavy-context batch scoring (up to 128k tokens in a single job, long-running, memory-bound) for our summarization pipeline.
2) Millisecond-scale interactive inference (reranking + short-chat) used in our product surface with tight p95 < 120ms.

We want a dedicated pool (reserved) to cover baseline throughput and a small burst pool for headroom. Can you recommend a SKU mix (H100, A100, L4) with an ops-friendly fallback plan and an order-of-magnitude monthly cost delta? Also uncertain about how much of the workload we can cache or shard to reduce memory pressure.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Gupta
VP Engineering, NovaAI

Attachments: nova_q3_demand_forecast.csv, NovaAI_SLA_requirements.pdf

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: dev_patel@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2028 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing request + forecast attached

Team — forwarding Nova's ask. Quick thoughts up front before we draft a response to Samir:

- Workload split implies two camps: memory-heavy long runs (summarization) and low-latency interactive. H100s are efficient for very large-context / memory-bound models; L4s are cheap and low-latency for small models and embeddings; A100 sits in the middle.
- Important to quantify concurrency vs. sequence length for the long jobs. If they submit many concurrent long jobs we need to reserve more H100 memory capacity or force queueing.
- We should propose a 3-pool design: Reserved H100 pool for large contexts (baseline capacity), Reserved A100 pool for mid-size models + fallback, and a larger L4 burstable pool for interactive traffic.

Can Dev run a quick slot/cost estimate based on the attached forecast? Neha: can you confirm what autoscale tolerance we can offer for their SLA (can we set burst headroom to 2x reserved for L4)? Dylan: any constraints on cache sizing for KV cache for long-context jobs?

I'll draft a recommendation for Samir once we have numbers.

— Priyom
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 15 Jun 2028 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated sizing request + forecast attached

Quick analysis (assumptions called out):
- Assumed models: long-context: Llama-3-70B-like at 80B params quantized (needs ~80GB NV memory for keys/activations per model instance for 128k context when using sharded KV strategies). Mid-size: Falcon-40B / 33B variants on A100 40GB. Interactive: distilled 7B / L4 class models.
- Throughput baseline from their CSV: baseline concurrent long jobs = 4 average, peak conc = 12; interactive avg qps = 600, peak = 1.6k.

Rough slot math (ballpark):
- H100-80GB (our H100-80 equivalent): one card can host 1 full long-context instance (single model) for 128k running at low concurrency; if we shard across 2 cards for perf headroom we get ~0.5 effective instances per card if we require <30s job latency. For 4 baseline conc -> need ~8 cards (with redundancy/overhead ~20% -> 10).
- A100-80GB / A100-40GB: great for 32k contexts / multitenant mid-size models. One A100-40 could serve ~3 mid-size inference slots for interactive-style mid-latency requests. For fallback capacity, plan 1:2 reserved:burst ratio.
- L4s: optimized for low-cost low-latency. Each L4 instance (infer-optimized) can handle ~150 qps for short-turn tasks (p95 < 120ms) depending on batching. For peak 1600 qps, reserve ~12 L4 units and allow burst to 36.

Preliminary suggested reserved mix (baseline to propose):
- H100: 10 reserved cards (baseline to support 4 concurrent long jobs with headroom).
- A100: 8 reserved cards (mid-size concurrency + can absorb some rps if L4 is saturated).
- L4: 12 reserved cards, burst pool up to +24 (total 36) for peak.

Cost sketch (net of discounts): 
- H100: approx $35/hr per card -> 10 cards reserved -> $8,400/month (assuming 720 hours) before reserved discounts.
- A100: approx $12/hr per card -> 8 cards -> $6,912/month.
- L4: approx $3.50/hr per card -> 12 cards -> $30,240/month.
(These are rough public-cloud-equivalent figures to help them compare; our actual committed pricing will be different.)

Ops notes:
- KV/prefix caching can reduce H100 pressure if we can cache common prefixes — recommend instrumenting a small pilot to measure hit rate; if >30% hit we could drop H100 reserved by ~2-3 cards.
- For tail latency: place L4s in same region and enable preferred routing; set auto-failover from L4->A100->H100 for specific endpoints (i.e., L4 handles short requests, A100 handles medium ones, H100 only used for explicit long-context jobs).

I'll put these numbers into the pricing spreadsheet and add a worst/best case scenario.

— Dev
Lead Inference Engineer, Redwood

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 16 Jun 2028 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated sizing request + forecast attached

Ops reality check:
- We can promise autoscale burst x2 for L4 with a 5-minute warm-up if they accept slightly higher p95 during spin-up. For guaranteed p95 windows (SLA) we should lock a minimum of L4 reserved.
- For H100s: immobilizing memory (pinned allocations) is needed for 128k contexts; that reduces effective slot density. Also add 10% capacity for maintenance and live migration.
- Networking: their batch jobs will have large checkpoint/IO traffic. Recommend network-attached NVMe staging in the same VPC to avoid cross-host penalties.

I'll add these ops constraints to the recommendation and include rollback runbook for when H100 jobs exceed memory limits (force queue + alert to engineering).

— Neha
Director of Operations, Redwood

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Samir Gupta <samir@novaai.com>, Procurement <procurement@novaai.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 17 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed dedicated pool mix and next steps (DEAL-8921)

Hi Samir — thanks for the details and the forecast. Based on the forecast and our internal sizing conversation (summary below), here is a recommended starting configuration and operational plan. Attaching the pricing scenario workbook.

Summary recommendation (reserved + burst):
- H100 (memory-first tier): 10 reserved cards + 2 spare (for maintenance) — reserved pool focused on long-context batch jobs. These are the only machines we recommend for 128k runs to avoid fragmentation.
- A100 (mid tier): 8 reserved cards — handles mid-size models and acts as the first fallback for interactive paths when L4 is saturated.
- L4 (low-latency): 12 reserved cards, burst to 36 (autoscale x3) — reserved to meet baseline p95 targets; burst handles marketing spikes and beta-day loads.

Operational and cost considerations:
- Cache pilot: run a 4-week KV/prefix caching pilot on 2 H100 cards to measure hit rate. If hit rate >30% we can reduce H100 reserved by ~2-3 cards and shift cost to A100/L4.
- Rollout: week 0–2: provision reserved pools; week 3: enable burst autoscale for L4; week 4–6: run load/chaos testing and adjust.
- Fallback policy: L4 -> A100 -> H100 only for requests labeled non-long-context. Long-context jobs must be scheduled to H100.
- Pricing: we provided best/likely/worst columns in attached workbook. Baseline expected infra spend (gross, before contract discounts): ~$160k/month. Final committed price will be negotiated in procurement and will include annual commit discounts.

Next steps:
1) Can procurement send preferred term lengths and target ARR for the commit? (Procurement)
2) Samir — any constraints on baseline p95 targets for the first 90 days?
3) Ops: I'll schedule a 30-minute sizing sync to finalize numbers and delivery timeline.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call.

— Priyom
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: pricing-scenario-h100-a100-l4.xlsx

- Procurement: we'll aim to get terms back by EOD Friday — any standard redlines we should be aware of (data residency, audit windows)?

If those items look ok we'll greenlight provisioning.
